# A workflow file holds the structure of its jobs, and nothing else

A file of `.github/workflows/` names its jobs, their triggers, their conditions, their runners and what they call.
No file holds the path filters: the `.github/workflows/ci.yaml#changes` job computes them when it runs, from each job's gate in `.github/ci-gates` and the `//ci:` lines of the tests (`.github/scripts/ci-filters-generate.sh`), and `dorny/paths-filter` reads the file it writes by path.
A `run:` body of more than 10 lines is a script under `.github/scripts/`, run by its path, with each budget comment on the line it sizes, but for two kinds of job.
A body stays inline where its job makes no checkout, and where its job holds a credential of a release workflow, as `release.yaml`'s publish job does, because `.github/scripts/check-release-credentials.sh` refuses a credentialed job that runs any script under a `scripts/` directory but `.github/scripts/release-push.sh` and `.github/scripts/check-private-names.sh`, each run by its path behind `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/`.
The longer bodies of `ci.yaml` are moved, and so are those of `dispatch-browser.yaml`, of `release.yaml` and of `ci-job-tool-fallback.yaml`, but for those two kinds of job.
The bodies of the other workflow files are not moved yet, and a file that reaches the size limit moves its bodies then, as the size check's refusal says.
A derivation or a history goes in `.github/ci-notes/<the workflow file's name without its suffix>.md`, and the step it belongs to keeps one comment line, `# why: .github/ci-notes/<file>.md#<the section's anchor>`, that names it; a value's own arithmetic stays on its line in the workflow file.
`.github/scripts/check-workflow-files.sh` holds every file of that directory to 64,000 bytes, and refuses one GitHub's own parser would not read (invalid YAML, or two keys of one mapping that are equal when upper-cased), one that calls more than 45 unique reusable workflows, one whose job or step sets `JOB_TIMEOUT_MINUTES` or `STEP_TIMEOUT_MINUTES` to anything but the `timeout-minutes` it stands for, or sets either where it stands for no one limit, one whose step has a `timeout-minutes` of its own, reaches `.github/scripts/gh-read.sh` and sets no `STEP_TIMEOUT_MINUTES` (that script waits for GitHub's rate limits within those numbers), and one with a Postgres service whose `command:` is not the line `.github/scripts/postgres-service-settings.sh --command` prints, or whose job has no step that runs that script with the service's container id to read the settings back (that script's header says what each setting costs or buys a test job); in ci.yaml and the workflows it calls, its rule 8 (`.github/scripts/go_test_steps.py`) also refuses a step that runs `go test`, itself or through a script it runs, other than through `.github/scripts/go_test_events.py`, such a step with no `id:` or with a `TEST_EVENTS_FILE` of its own, a job that does not upload those steps' events after them with `.github/actions/go-test-events-upload`, which names the artifact `go-test-events-<job id>` (docs/testing.md, "Which tests a CI job ran"), and, in the ci-filters job, which hands it the filters the changes job computed, a step whose script the `ci_filters` filter does not select (`.github/ci-gates/ci-filters.py` says why that filter reads those scripts).
The number is 64,000 because GitHub starts no run at all for a workflow file above its cap of 500 KB and signals that only as a run with no jobs in it, so the limit a reader is held to is a readable file rather than a parser's limit.
The `.github/workflows/ci.yaml#ci-filters` job runs the check, `.github/workflows/workflow-files.yaml` runs it a second time in a file small enough to start when `ci.yaml` is too large to, and `ci.yaml`'s test job runs `.github/scripts/check-workflow-files.test.sh` and, for rule 8, `.github/scripts/go_test_steps.test.sh`.
actionlint 1.7.12 checks every workflow file in those same two places, with `.github/actionlint.yaml`, and the shellcheck 0.11.0 it hands each inline `run:` body reads at warning severity, so a finding of either fails the pull request.
Run what CI runs before you push a workflow change, from the root of a git checkout, since actionlint finds no project outside one: `SHELLCHECK_OPTS=--severity=warning go run github.com/rhysd/actionlint/cmd/actionlint@v1.7.12 -shellcheck='uvx --from shellcheck-py@0.11.0.1 shellcheck' -verbose`
